title: The DIC 8-Year Provision
content:
**Rule.** The 8-year provision of Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) applies only when the rating record shows the veteran rated totally disabled for the 8-year provision period immediately before death while married to the spouse throughout.

When the 8-year provision is established, the award's rate category changes to the matching category "with 8-Year Provision" — DIC Surviving Spouse (Basic Rate with 8-Year Provision), DIC Surviving Spouse (Housebound with 8-Year Provision) or DIC Surviving Spouse (Aid and Attendance with 8-Year Provision).

### The parts of the condition

1. **Source of proof** — the veteran's rating record. The surviving spouse's own account of the veteran's disability is not what the rule looks to.
2. **Level of rating** — rated totally disabled.
3. **Period** — the 8-year provision period, ending immediately before the death.
4. **Marriage** — the spouse was married to the veteran throughout that period.

### When the condition fails

Because the provision applies *only* when all four parts are shown, a failure of any one part means the 8-year provision does not apply:

| Rating record shows total disability | For the full period immediately before death | Married throughout that period | 8-year provision |
|---|---|---|---|
| No | — | — | Does not apply |
| Yes | No | — | Does not apply |
| Yes | Yes | No | Does not apply |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | The condition of this rule is satisfied |

### Questions the rule answers

**The veteran was totally disabled for the whole period, but the rating record shows a total rating for only part of it. Does the provision apply?** No. The rule turns on what the rating record shows.

**The rating record shows a total rating for the full period, but it ended some years before the death. Does the provision apply?** No. The period must run immediately before the death.

**The couple married partway through the period of total rating. Does the provision apply?** No. The spouse must have been married to the veteran throughout the period.
